shots.loi: Could Prime Michael Vick scramble out
of the destruction of Pompeii? In 2006, Michael Vick rushed
for 1 ,039 yards,
becoming the first quarterback in
NFL history to break 1 ,000.
Defenses knew he was running. It didn't help.
Meanwhile, in 79 AD,
Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii beneath
volcanic ash and falling pumice.
Eventually, a deadly cloud of superheated gas swept
through the city. So, naturally, Vick is given a football and
told to reach the city gates. He takes the snap in the Roman forum.
A collapsing rooftop blocks the right side. Vick rolls left. Three Roman soldiers fill the alley. Vick plants his foot,
cuts outside.
All three lose contain.
First down,
the ash thickens. An overturned wagon blocks the street.
Vick reverses field and
cuts through a Roman house.
At the entrance, a mosaic reads Cave
Canem, Latin
for beware of the dog.
Six guard dogs block the exit.
For once, Vick decides against
a dog fight. He
cuts back through the courtyard, finds
an open alley, and sprints toward the city gates. The dogs follow.
Vick crosses the gate just before the ash cloud arrives. Final stat line,
184 rushing yards, zero sacks, and six dogs successfully evacuated.
The dogs are immediately placed in protective custody.
